records.source: The ``measurement_units`` value of the rows being described — one of :data:`MEASUREMENT_UNITS`. Geometric columns have no single unit any more (a 3-D run measures a volume, in micrometres when it was given a voxel size), so pass this when you know it and the returned ``unit`` is concrete. Left ``None``, ``unit`` states every possibility with the condition attached rather than guessing one; :func:`describe_database` fills it in from the database itself.
records.translation: ``measurement_units``-gildi línanna sem lýst er — eitt af :data:`MEASUREMENT_UNITS`. Rúmfræðilegir dálkar hafa ekki lengur eina einingu (3-D keyrsla mælir rúmmál, í míkrómetrum þegar hún fékk rúmpixlastærð), svo sendið þetta þegar það er þekkt og ``unit`` sem skilað er verður ákveðin. Ef það er látið vera ``None`` tilgreinir ``unit`` alla möguleika með skilyrðinu áföstu frekar en að giska á einn; :func:`describe_database` fyllir það út úr gagnagrunninum sjálfum.

records.context: The script serves three purposes, and the third is why it also carries a data structure:
records.label: spacr.macro#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The script serves three purposes, and the third is why it also carries a data structure:
records.translation: Forskriftin þjónar þremur tilgangi, og sá þriðji er ástæðan fyrir því að hún ber líka gagnaskipan:

records.context: **A reproducibility record.** The script is the method section. Its header carries the spaCR version, the processing-session id and the settings hash. The processing-session id is the id :mod:`spacr.runctx` stamped on every log line the processing session emitted and :mod:`spacr.artifacts` stamped on every output it registered, so the script, the log and the files all join on one column. The settings hash is :func:`spacr.artifacts.settings_hash`, the same digest the artifact rows carry.
records.label: spacr.macro#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A reproducibility record.** The script is the method section. Its header carries the spaCR version, the run id and the settings hash. The run id is the id :mod:`spacr.runctx` stamped on every log line the run emitted and :mod:`spacr.artifacts` stamped on every output it registered, so the script, the log and the files all join on one column. The settings hash is :func:`spacr.artifacts.settings_hash`, the same digest the artifact rows carry.
records.translation: **Skráning fyrir endurtakanleika.** Forskriftin er aðferðakaflinn. Haus hennar ber spaCR-útgáfuna, auðkenni keyrslunnar og tætigildi stillinganna. Auðkenni keyrslunnar er auðkennið sem :mod:`spacr.runctx` stimplaði á hverja annálslínu sem keyrslan gaf út og :mod:`spacr.artifacts` stimplaði á hvert úttak sem hún skráði, svo forskriftin, annállinn og skrárnar tengjast allar á einum dálki. Tætigildi stillinganna er :func:`spacr.artifacts.settings_hash`, sama tætigildi og línur afurðanna bera.

records.context: **A starting point for the Python API.** ``macro.py`` holds the code a user would write by hand — the import and the entry-point call — rather than a wrapper or a replay harness.
records.label: spacr.macro#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A starting point for the Python API.** ``macro.py`` holds the code a user would write by hand — the import and the entry-point call — rather than a wrapper or a replay harness.
records.translation: **Upphafspunktur fyrir Python API.** ``macro.py`` geymir kóðann sem notandi myndi skrifa handvirkt — innflutninginn og kallið á inngangsstaðinn — frekar en umgjörð eða endurspilunarkerfi.

records.context: **Most of the input to the methods-and-results exporter.** Which is why the script also carries :data:`MACRO`, a plain key-value mapping literal holding every step's module, entry point, processing-session id, settings, which of those settings were merely defaults, what it produced and how long it took. :func:`read_macro` reads it back *without executing the script* — it is parsed, not imported — so the exporter can consume a macro it did not generate and does not trust.
records.label: spacr.macro#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Most of the input to the methods-and-results exporter.** Which is why the script also carries :data:`MACRO`, a plain dict literal holding every step's module, entry point, run id, settings, which of those settings were merely defaults, what it produced and how long it took. :func:`read_macro` reads it back *without executing the script* — it is parsed, not imported — so the exporter can consume a macro it did not generate and does not trust.
records.translation: **Mestur hluti inntaksins í útflytjanda aðferða og niðurstaðna.** Þess vegna ber forskriftin líka :data:`MACRO`, einfalda orðabókarlesningu sem geymir einingu hvers skrefs, inngangsstað, keyrsluauðkenni, stillingar, hverjar þeirra stillinga voru aðeins sjálfgefnar, hvað það framleiddi og hve langan tíma það tók. :func:`read_macro` les hana til baka *án þess að keyra forskriftina* — hún er þáttuð, ekki flutt inn — svo útflytjandinn getur notað fjölva sem hann bjó ekki til og treystir ekki.

So this walks the AST, evaluates the top-level literal assignments (which is how the ``PROJECT_1`` and ``*_SETTINGS`` names the metadata refers to are resolved) and returns the record.
records.translation: Þáttað, aldrei keyrt. Inntak útflytjandans er skrá sem spaCR hefur kannski ekki skrifað — fjölvi einhvers annars, breyttur fjölvi, einn úr nýrri útgáfu — og innflutningur hennar myndi keyra hvað sem í henni er. Því gengur þetta í gegnum AST, metur úthlutanir lesninga á efsta stigi (sem er hvernig heitin ``PROJECT_1`` og ``*_SETTINGS`` sem lýsigögnin vísa í eru leyst) og skilar færslunni.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A measurements database stamped ``pplate1`` produces merged rows stamped ``pplate1``, while the score and count CSVs have already been normalised to ``plate1``. The two then do not meet. Every join inside the merge is unaffected, because both sides read the same stored value, so the merge succeeds with the right row counts and the failure appears later, in a downstream join.
records.translation: Mælingagagnagrunnur stimplaður ``pplate1`` framleiðir sameinaðar línur stimplaðar ``pplate1``, á meðan einkunna- og talningar-CSV-skrárnar hafa þegar verið staðlaðar í ``plate1``. Þetta tvennt mætist þá ekki. Hver samtenging innan sameiningarinnar er óbreytt, því báðar hliðar lesa sama vistaða gildið, svo sameiningin tekst með réttan fjölda lína og villan birtist síðar, í síðari samtengingu.

records.translation: Samsettir lyklar eru líka staðlaðir. ``prc`` er ``<plate>_<row>_<column>``, svo tvöfalt forskeyti ferðast í fyrsta hluta hans; ef aðeins ``plateID`` væri endurskrifað yrði ekki hægt að tengja ``prc`` og dálkarnir tveir yrðu ósammála um sömu plötuna.

records.context: **Sign convention.**  The R computes ``mean_inv = -mean``, recodes ``hit`` as a factor with levels ``c("no", "yes")``, and hands both to ``yardstick``. ``yardstick``'s default ``event_level`` is ``"first"``, so the event it scores is ``"no"`` — the *non*-hits — and the score it scores them with is ``-mean``.  Scoring ``-m`` for the event "not a hit" is identical to scoring ``+m`` for the event "is a hit": both ROC curves are the same curve.  This port computes the equivalent ``roc_auc_score(y_true=hit, y_score=mean)``, and :func:`spacr.power_model.evaluate_model_fit`'s tests pin the orientation on a case whose answer is known — strong planted hits must score near 1, not near 0.  A flipped convention returns ``1 - AUROC``, which for a mediocre design is a plausible-looking value.
records.label: spacr.power_model.evaluate_model_fit#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Sign convention.**  The R computes ``mean_inv = -mean``, recodes ``hit`` as a factor with levels ``c("no", "yes")``, and hands both to ``yardstick``. ``yardstick``'s default ``event_level`` is ``"first"``, so the event it scores is ``"no"`` — the *non*-hits — and the score it scores them with is ``-mean``.  Scoring ``-m`` for the event "not a hit" is identical to scoring ``+m`` for the event "is a hit": both ROC curves are the same curve.  This port computes the equivalent ``roc_auc_score(y_true=hit, y_score=mean)``, and :func:`spacr.power_model.evaluate_model_fit`'s tests pin the orientation on a case whose answer is known — strong planted hits must score near 1, not near 0.  A flipped convention returns ``1 - AUROC``, which for a mediocre design is a plausible-looking value.
records.translation: **Formerkjavenja.**  R reiknar ``mean_inv = -mean``, endurkóðar ``hit`` sem þátt með stigunum ``c("no", "yes")``, og afhendir hvort tveggja ``yardstick``. Í ``yardstick`` er sjálfgefið ``event_level`` ``"first"``, svo atburðurinn sem það metur er ``"no"`` — *ekki*-smellirnir — og einkunnin sem það metur þá með er ``-mean``.  Að meta ``-m`` fyrir atburðinn "not a hit" er það sama og að meta ``+m`` fyrir atburðinn "is a hit": báðir ROC-ferlarnir eru sami ferillinn.  Þessi útgáfa reiknar jafngilda ``roc_auc_score(y_true=hit, y_score=mean)``, og prófanir :func:`spacr.power_model.evaluate_model_fit` festa stefnuna á tilviki þar sem svarið er þekkt — sterkir gróðursettir smellir verða að fá einkunn nálægt 1, ekki nálægt 0.  Snúin venja skilar ``1 - AUROC``, sem fyrir miðlungs hönnun er trúverðugt gildi.

records.context: Returning exactly ``False`` stops the sweep and returns the rows completed so far; anything else (including ``None``) continues. records.source: Three rules govern what it does:
records.translation: Þrjár reglur stýra því sem hún gerir:

records.context: **A missing section is stated, never omitted.** If segmentation QC was never executed, the report contains a "Segmentation QC" heading that says *not executed*. A reader cannot distinguish "clean" from "never checked" if unchecked things silently vanish, and that is exactly how a partial run gets forwarded as though it were complete.
records.label: spacr.report#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A missing section is stated, never omitted.** If segmentation QC was never run, the report contains a "Segmentation QC" heading that says *not run*. A reader cannot distinguish "clean" from "never checked" if unchecked things silently vanish, and that is exactly how a partial run gets forwarded as though it were complete.
records.translation: **Hluti sem vantar er tilgreindur, aldrei sleppt.** Ef QC bútunar var aldrei keyrt inniheldur skýrslan "Segmentation QC"-fyrirsögn sem segir *ekki keyrt*. Lesandi getur ekki greint "clean" frá "never checked" ef óathugaðir hlutir hverfa hljóðlega, og það er einmitt hvernig keyrsla að hluta er send áfram eins og hún væri heil.

records.context: **Failure goes at the top.** :mod:`spacr.errors` stamps every artifact with a ``run_status`` recording how many items failed. If anything failed — or if nothing was stamped at all, so completeness is unknown — that is the first thing in the document, not an appendix entry.
records.label: spacr.report#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Failure goes at the top.** :mod:`spacr.errors` stamps every artifact with a ``run_status`` recording how many items failed. If anything failed — or if nothing was stamped at all, so completeness is unknown — that is the first thing in the document, not an appendix entry.
records.translation: **Villa fer efst.** :mod:`spacr.errors` stimplar hverja afurð með ``run_status`` sem skráir hve mörg atriði mistókust. Ef eitthvað mistókst — eða ef ekkert var stimplað yfirleitt, svo heilleiki er óþekktur — er það það fyrsta í skjalinu, ekki færsla í viðauka.

records.context: spaCR depends on matplotlib and on nothing that converts HTML to PDF, and this module will not add such a dependency for one feature. The PDF is therefore a **monospace transcription** of the same content — the same sections, the same tables, the same "not run" statements — plus one page per embedded figure. Compared with the HTML it loses colour emphasis, table borders, collapsible detail blocks and clickable contents, and long cells are truncated to the page width. Send the HTML when the recipient can open one.
records.label: spacr.report.write_pdf#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: spaCR depends on matplotlib and on nothing that converts HTML to PDF, and this module will not add such a dependency for one feature. The PDF is therefore a **monospace transcription** of the same content — the same sections, the same tables, the same "not run" statements — plus one page per embedded figure. Compared with the HTML it loses colour emphasis, table borders, collapsible detail blocks and clickable contents, and long cells are truncated to the page width. Send the HTML when the recipient can open one.
records.translation: spaCR er háð matplotlib og engu sem breytir HTML í PDF, og þessi eining mun ekki bæta slíku ósjálfstæði við fyrir einn eiginleika. PDF-skjalið er því **jafnbreið afritun** sama innihalds — sömu hlutar, sömu töflur, sömu "not run"-yfirlýsingar — auk einnar síðu á hverja innfellda mynd. Miðað við HTML tapar það litaáherslu, töfluramma, samfellanlegum smáatriðablokkum og smellanlegu efnisyfirliti, og langir reitir eru styttir við breidd síðunnar. Sendið HTML þegar viðtakandinn getur opnað slíka skrá.

records.translation: Knýr innsýnarmælaborð heimaskjásins: ``total_runs`` (allar skrár yfir innihald sem sáust), ``mask_runs`` / ``measure_runs`` / ``classify_runs`` (fjöldi eftir forriti) og ``models_recorded`` (aðgreind tætigildi líkana sem nokkurn tíma hafa verið skráð, yfir keyrslur allra forrita — ekki aðeins mask-keyrslur). Skilar núllum þegar engin dagbók er enn til.

records.context: Counting is incremental: the totals and the names of the folders already counted are persisted in ``.journal_totals.json`` in the processing-session root, so each call parses only the manifests it has not seen. A folder that has since been deleted cannot be subtracted, so that case falls back to a full recount. A manifest that cannot be parsed is left out of the totals with a logged warning.
records.label: spacr.run_journal.journal_totals#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Counting is incremental: the totals and the names of the folders already counted are persisted in ``.journal_totals.json`` in the runs root, so each call parses only the manifests it has not seen. A folder that has since been deleted cannot be subtracted, so that case falls back to a full recount. A manifest that cannot be parsed is left out of the totals with a logged warning.
records.translation: Talning er stigvaxandi: heildartölurnar og heiti mappanna sem þegar hafa verið taldar eru vistuð í ``.journal_totals.json`` í rót keyrslnanna, svo hvert kall þáttar aðeins skrár yfir innihald sem það hefur ekki séð. Mappa sem síðan hefur verið eytt er ekki hægt að draga frá, svo það tilvik fellur til baka á fulla endurtalningu. Skrá yfir innihald sem ekki er hægt að þátta er sleppt úr heildartölunum með viðvörun í annál.
